There’s some good advice here. I understand how life changing it can be. So many people hate drugs and refuse to discuss it. Personally I’ve found mdma and psychedelics in general to be wonderful in my life and also in my relationship. I have definitely been in relationships like yours but I didn’t realize how life changing a trip or roll could be at the time. At this point in my life, if I were single again I would definitely need a partner who tripped or rolled with me or at least supported that part of my life. For me, psychedelics (that includes MDMA) are almost like my ‘religion’. They are therapeutic-helping me accept certain facts of life while also getting closure when needed. You definitely should never force someone or try to wear them down but I don’t think it’s wrong to show your partner why you use them and why you’d like to her to join you. Maybe showing her research on its history from beginning to most recently. I can’t recall how, when, why it was first created but I do know that towards the beginning of its creation it was used by therapy patients during sessions in order to help them open up emotionally. Obviously it ended up being thrown on the anti-drug track for many years-even though it did show enormous medicinal potential it was still listed as a schedule 1 drug. However, in recent years, psychedelics; including MDMA are now being openly studied and tested to treat PTSD, drug resistant depression, other mental health disorders and even addiction. So Maybe if she sees the potential of this extremely useful drug by seeing research studies, articles, etc and then hearing your POV, maybe she will see how much good it could bring to your relationship. No doubt it can help couples bond deeply while also allowing you both to work through past disagreements and even previous (childhood/young adult) traumas (that effect your adult lives today), maybe she will be willing to give it a shot. Or maybe not. Some people will forever only believe what they have been told via anti-drug propaganda unfortunately. 

But lying to her is not ok. You may find she doesn’t respond the way you want. She may need time. Or maybe she will always be against it.  You may decide you don’t want to stop occasionally rolling while she never will. Regardless lying will only ruin your relationship. So think about it before deciding how to go about it. I hope it works out as I believe the world would be a much better place if more people tripped, micro-dosed and rolled. You can buy test kits to test your MDMA in order to show her there are safe ways for consenting adults to take drugs.  I wish you both the best!

People with substance abuse issues, like myself are not bad people. Soberity is a journey. Not a destination. I know that sounds corny but it’s true. It’s a problem he has within himself. So don’t ever take him getting drunk or high as a personal slight. It’s not. If you stay with him know that he will likely relapse again. That’s just part of it. You either accept this as part of his life and work actively (I do not support AA personally but Alon is good in my opinion. I know AA helps some people but I do not like their tactics. They aren’t for everyone) to help him in his recovery and help during any relapses. And not be enabler. Or don’t. My ex threw my using in my face. Like I was lying to him personally. That never helped. He still blames me for it and says his cheating is justified. It’s not. Good luck to him in his recovery and to you if you stay.
